en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks spoke with food still in their mouths... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not speak with food in my mouth.
One must not speak with food in one's mouth."
Whoever, out of disrespect, speaks with food still in his mouth, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional … [and so forth] …
The third training rule is concluded.
